```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 16_factorial_anova_design
title: >
  Come up with a 2x2 Design
questions:
  - id: two_by_two_design
    type: free-response
    prompt: >
      Come up with a two-by-two design: two independent variables with two levels
      each, and one dependent variable.
    answer: >
      A good answer names Factor A with two levels, Factor B with two levels, and a
      dependent variable measured in all four resulting conditions.
    explanation: >
      For example: caffeine (coffee vs decaf) by sleep (short vs full night),
      measuring reaction time.

  - id: sketch_prediction
    type: figure
    responseFrom: designInteraction.sketch
    prompt: >
      Now sketch the result you'd predict. Call your first independent variable
      Factor A and your second Factor B. Each dot is the mean of one of your
      four groups. Drag each one up or down to roughly where you'd expect it to
      be. Your graph is saved automatically.
    figure: |
      {{< interactive-figure designInteraction makeInteractionPlot options='{"means":{"a1b1":4,"a2b1":4,"a1b2":6,"a2b2":6},"draggable":true,"controls":false,"step":1,"valueLabels":true,"yTicks":"numeric","yLabel":"Your dependent variable","maxWidth":"34rem","ariaLabel":"Interaction plot of four group means that can each be dragged up or down: A1 and A2 on the x axis, with one line for B1 and one for B2."}' fallback="An interaction plot with four draggable group means: the B1 line starts flat at 4 and the B2 line flat at 6. Enable JavaScript to sketch your own result." >}}

  - id: sketch_effects
    type: multiple-select
    contextFrom: designInteraction.sketch
    prompt: >
      Look at the graph you just made. Going only by where the four means are,
      which of these does it show?
    options:
      - text: A main effect of Factor A
        correctFrom: designInteraction.showsMainEffectA
      - text: A main effect of Factor B
        correctFrom: designInteraction.showsMainEffectB
      - text: An interaction between Factor A and Factor B
        correctFrom: designInteraction.showsInteraction
      - text: None of these
        correctFrom: designInteraction.showsNoEffects
    hints:
      - >
        For Factor A, picture the point midway between the two dots above
        $A_1$, and the point midway between the two dots above $A_2$. Is one
        higher than the other?
      - >
        For Factor B, compare the middle of one line with the middle of the
        other. For the interaction, check whether the lines are parallel.
    explanation: >
      On your graph, the marginal means for Factor A are
      <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.marginalA1" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at $A_1$ and
      <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.marginalA2" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at $A_2$. If those
      differ, there's a main effect of Factor A. The marginal means for
      Factor B are <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.marginalB1" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at
      $B_1$ and <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.marginalB2" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at
      $B_2$. If those differ, there's a main effect of Factor B. And going
      from $A_1$ to $A_2$ changes the mean by
      <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.effectAatB1" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at $B_1$ and by
      <span class="interactive-value" data-interactive-value="designInteraction.effectAatB2" data-interactive-empty="...">...</span> at $B_2$. If
      those differ, the lines aren't parallel, and that's an interaction.
      Remember that this is only the pattern in the means. Whether any of it
      would be statistically significant depends on the variability within
      the groups too.

  - id: sketch_explain
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Save response
    prompt: >
      In a sentence or two, put the pattern in your graph into words, in terms
      of your own study. If your graph shows an interaction, try starting with
      "The effect of ... depends on ...".
    explanation: >
      A good answer describes the pattern in terms of what was manipulated and
      measured, not just "Factor A" and "Factor B". It says which main effects
      it shows and in which direction, and whether the effect of one factor is
      the same at both levels of the other.
```
